entries.verification_note: The 2024 AR1000F and AR1000NR instructions (https://www.dfa.arkansas.gov/wp-content/uploads/2024_AR1000F_and_AR1000NR_Instructions.pdf, sha256 dcaab308e4c47b372a0f51acbf0eae42d0be006426ee83ab989bf59f19fe9297, retrieved 2026-11-10) state a standard deduction of $2,410 for single, head of household, married filing separately, and surviving spouse, and $4,820 for married filing joint. The held deduction is $2,340 single / $4,680 joint. The DFA What's New page (https://www.dfa.arkansas.gov/office/taxes/income-tax-administration/individual-income-tax/whats-new/, sha256 bfebef988d7dfff61159b531f501f908d705b27d160bce36c5fac7196ab3a0fc, retrieved 2026-11-10) states the 2023 standard deduction is $2,340 for those statuses and $4,680 for filing status 2. The 2024 instructions do not print the bracket thresholds. https://www.dfa.arkansas.gov/wp-content/uploads/2025_TaxBrackets.pdf (sha256 a54fb139ba2b997b5545217474a0558c94e943f62f5d089c81299a81e30c9f02, retrieved 2026-11-02) states 2025 brackets of 0% to $5,599, 2% to $11,199, 3% to $15,999, 3.4% to $26,399, and 3.9% above that. Those match the held 2025 brackets. The same PDF prints a bracket-adjustment band from $94,701 to $97,800, where the 3.9% minus-adjustment steps down, and for $100,001 and over a formula of $3,809 plus 3.9% of the excess over $100,000. That band is not modeled.
